hook.speaker: Krishna (quoted by Bhishma)
hook.setting: Krishna, tired of feuds in his own clan, confides in the sage Narada and asks how to keep the peace.
hook.sanskrit: अरणीमग्निकामो वा मथ्नाति दहृयं मम / वाचा दुरुक्तं देवर्षे तन्मां दहति नित्यदा
hook.line: Harsh words from family can keep burning long after they're said. Even Krishna felt it.
hook.translation: My heart is churned the way someone wanting fire churns a fire-stick. The harsh words my relatives say keep burning me, day after day.
hook.why: In family feuds, the weapon that works is gentleness, patience and respect.

prasang.title: Krishna's family troubles: the weapon not made of iron
prasang.summary: Even Krishna struggles with his clan: he does their work, bears their harsh words, and feels like the mother of two gamblers playing each other. Narada tells him the only weapon that works is soft: generosity, patience, sincerity, gentleness and respect.
prasang.story_hook: Krishna, who guided a war, admitted to a sage that he could not keep the peace in his own family.
prasang.lesson: In family feuds, the weapon that works is gentleness, patience and respect.

hook.for_you: You feel like you'll never be loved without being abandoned, and the harsh words of your own kin keep churning your heart like a fire stick.

alternates.speaker: Bharata
alternates.setting: Grieving Kausalya accuses Bharata of plotting Ram's exile; he knew nothing of it.
alternates.sanskrit: आर्ये कस्मादजानन्तं गर्हसे मामकल्मषम्। विपुलां च मम प्रीतिं स्थितां जानासि राघवे॥
alternates.line: Why blame me, who knew nothing? You know what I feel for him.
alternates.translation: Noble lady, why do you blame me, who knew nothing and did nothing wrong? You know how deep my love for Ram is.
alternates.why: Being blamed for what you did not do hurts most from those you love; stay and make your truth known.

prasang.title: Bharata wrongly blamed
prasang.summary: Bharata turns on his mother in fury. Then Ram's grieving mother assumes he plotted it all, and her words cut him like a needle in a wound. He falls at her feet and swears his innocence until she believes him.
prasang.story_hook: He had done nothing, and the one person whose good opinion he needed was sure he had done it all.
prasang.lesson: Being blamed for what you did not do hurts most from those you love; stay and make your truth known.

alternates.speaker: Bharat
alternates.setting: After fourteen years, Hanuman brings Bharat the news that Ram is coming; Bharat has one question.
alternates.sanskrit: तब हनुमंत नाइ पद माथा। कहे सकल रघुपति गुन गाथा॥ कहु कपि कबहुँ कृपाल गोसाईं। सुमिरहिं मोहि दास की नाईं ॥
alternates.line: Tell me: does he ever think of me?
alternates.translation: Then Hanuman bowed at his feet and told all of Raghupati's virtues. 'Tell me, Hanuman: does the kind master ever remember me, as one remembers a servant?'

verse.ref: Mahabharata · Shanti Parva · Shanti: Consolation of Yudhishthira
verse.speaker: Ashma (quoted by Vyasa)
verse.setting: The sage Ashma answers King Janaka, who asks how to stay steady when people and wealth come and go.
verse.sanskrit: मानसानां पुनर्योनिर्दुःखानां चित्तविभ्रमः / अनिष्टोपनिपातो वा तृतीयं नोपपद्यते
verse.line: Mental pain comes from two places: something you didn't want happened, or your mind is spinning. No third.
verse.translation: Sorrow of the mind has only two sources: a confused, wandering mind, or something unwanted happening to you. There is no third.
verse.why: Days don't come back. Grieve, then steady yourself with the people still in front of you.

prasang.title: Ashma Gita: the sage on bearing loss
prasang.summary: Vyasa tells the grieving Yudhishthira how the sage Ashma consoled King Janaka: pain comes from what we didn't want or what we lost; meetings end; days don't return; ask who you are and steady the mind.
prasang.lesson: Days don't come back. Grieve, then steady yourself with the people still in front of you.

verse.for_you: Something someone did stays with you. The mind then spins around that hurt, adding pain to the wound. You can notice when the mind is wandering, and let the first hurt be just what it is.
verse.try_today: Notice when the mind is spinning and let it rest for a moment.
verse.scene_line: You sit with your books, and the mind adds pain to the hurt that already happened.

why: Two sources of the mind's pain (Mahabharata, Shanti Parva (Ashma Gita))
Sorts the pain into what happened and what the mind is adding

verse.speaker: Seer
verse.setting: The creation story: last of all, dharma is made.
verse.sanskrit: स नैव व्यभवत् तच्छ्रेयो रूपमत्यसृजत धर्मम् । तदेतत्क्षत्रस्य क्षत्रं यद्धर्मस्तस्माद्धर्मात् परं नास्त्यथो अबलीयान् बलीयाꣳसमाशꣳसते धर्मेण यथा राज्ञैवम् । यो वै स धर्मः सत्यं वै तत् तस्मात्सत्यं वदन्तमाहुर्धर्मं वदतीति धर्मं वा वदन्तꣳ सत्यं वदतीत्येतद्ध्येवैतदुभयं भवति ॥
verse.line: Nothing is higher than what is right. With it the weak can face the strong. What is right is truth.
verse.translation: Still he did not flourish. So he created a higher form, dharma. Dharma is the power over power; nothing is higher than dharma. Through dharma even a weak man can stand up to a strong one, as with the help of a king. That dharma is truth. So people say of one who speaks truth, 'He speaks dharma,' and of one who speaks dharma, 'He speaks truth.' Both are the same.
verse.why: Fear and loneliness are human; truth gives even the weak a footing.

prasang.title: The first being: fear, loneliness and dharma
prasang.summary: In this creation story the first being, alone, feels fear, then realises there is no one else to fear. He feels no joy alone and longs for a companion, splitting into husband and wife. Finally dharma is created, the truth by which even the weak can stand up to the strong.
prasang.lesson: Fear and loneliness are human; truth gives even the weak a footing.

verse.for_you: Something someone did stays with you, and you feel like you will never be loved without being abandoned. Rightness is the only power that does not leave, and truth is its name. Stand in that truth today.
verse.try_today: Notice one moment today when you choose to speak what is right, even if no one is watching.

why: the weaker party is not without standing
With what is right the weak can face the strong.

verse.speaker: Lakshman
verse.setting: Sita has been taken; Lakshman, the younger brother, gently tries to bring Ram back to himself.
verse.sanskrit: बुद्धिश्च ते महाप्राज्ञ देवैरपि दुरन्वया। शोकेनाभिप्रसुप्तं ते ज्ञानं सम्बोधयाम्यहम्॥
verse.line: Your wisdom isn't gone. Grief has only put it to sleep for a while.
verse.translation: Your understanding, wise one, is beyond even the gods' reckoning. Grief has only put your wisdom to sleep, and I am here to wake it.
verse.for_you: Someone left a mark on you that still hurts. That pain is not the end of your story. Your own clear mind is waiting for you to return to it.
verse.try_today: Notice the feeling of being abandoned, then name one thing you already understand about it.

why: he is told he is not broken
Feelings come and go, bear them; your wisdom is asleep, not gone (Lakshmana to Rama).

verse.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
verse.line: The remedy for weakness is not brooding over weakness, but thinking of strength.
verse.translation: But, says the Vedanta, being reminded of weakness does not help much; give strength, and strength does not come by thinking of weakness all the time. The remedy for weakness is not brooding over weakness, but thinking of strength.
verse.why: Stop rehearsing your weakness; think of your strength and act.

prasang.title: Practical Vedanta 1: faith in yourself (London, 1896)
prasang.summary: Vedanta must work in ordinary life. Calm minds do the most work, angry ones break themselves. The new religion calls the person who does not believe in himself the atheist, and the remedy for weakness is to think of strength, not brood over weakness.
prasang.lesson: Stop rehearsing your weakness; think of your strength and act.

verse.for_you: You feel like you will never be loved without being abandoned. That pain is real. Strength lives in you even now.
verse.try_today: Notice one thing you did well today without dwelling on what went wrong.

why: Think of strength, not of weakness.
turn the mind to what is strong in you

verse.speaker: Vidula
verse.setting: Queen Vidula rouses her son, who lies defeated and despairing after losing his kingdom.
verse.sanskrit: उद्यम्य धुरमुत्कर्षेदाजानेयकृतं स्मरन् / कुरु सत्वं च मानं च विद्धि पौरुषमात्मनः
verse.line: Pick up the load again. Summon your strength and self-respect, and know the power in you.
verse.translation: Lift the load and pull it forward, remembering how a thoroughbred works. Summon your strength and your self-respect; know the power that is in you.
verse.why: Past failure doesn't define you. Results are uncertain, but those who never try never succeed.

prasang.title: Vidula rouses her defeated son
prasang.summary: Kunti sends Yudhishthira the old story of Queen Vidula, who finds her son lying defeated after losing his kingdom. She shames, then reasons, then encourages him until he rises and fights for it again.
prasang.story_hook: A prince lay in bed after losing everything, until his mother walked in and refused to let him stay there.
prasang.lesson: Past failure doesn't define you. Results are uncertain, but those who never try never succeed.

verse.for_you: Something someone did stays with you. You feel like you will never be loved without being abandoned. Pick up the load again. Summon your strength and know the power that is already in you.
verse.try_today: Notice one thing today that proves your strength is still yours.
verse.scene_line: You stand in the ruins of your trust, while Sanjaya lies defeated, both called to rise.

why: Mana, self-respect, is to be summoned

story.title: Karna comes alone to the man who insulted him
story.story_hook: Karna waited until everyone had left. Then he went to the dying man who had insulted him for twenty years.
story.summary: For years the old commander belittled him in open court, and Karna swore not to fight while Bhishma led. Now Bhishma lies on the arrows, the crowd has gone, and Karna comes in the dark, falls at his feet and says, his voice breaking: I am Radha's son, the one you always looked at with dislike.
story.lesson: A harsh word can come from concern, and an old quarrel can be ended at a deathbed without either side giving up what he stands for.
story.teaser: Karna waited until everyone had left. Then he went to the dying man who had insulted him for twenty years.
story.for_you: The words that hurt you still sit in your chest. They do not have to be the final word. You can carry them without letting them define you.

verse.speaker: Tulsidas
verse.setting: Bharat walks toward Ram, slowed by shame, quickened by love.
verse.sanskrit: फेरति मनहुँ मातु कृत खोरी। चलत भगति बल धीरज धोरी॥ जब समुझत रघुनाथ सुभाऊ। तब पथ परत उताइल पाऊ ॥
verse.line: Shame slowed him. But whenever he remembered Ram's nature, his feet moved faster.
verse.translation: It was as if his mother's wrong held him back, while the strength of devotion drove him on like a patient ox. Whenever he remembered Raghunath's nature, his feet moved faster on the path.

why: his feet are pulled back by a wrong that was not his
Everyone must think I wanted this. I can't look at anyone. Will he even see me?

verse.speaker: Kakbhushundi
verse.setting: Garuda's last question is about the diseases of the mind; Kakbhushundi answers.
verse.sanskrit: मोह सकल ब्याधिन्ह कर मूला। तिन्ह ते पुनि उपजहिं बहु सूला॥ काम बात कफ लोभ अपारा। क्रोध पित्त नित छाती जारा ॥
verse.line: Confusion is the root illness. Anger is the bile that keeps your chest burning.
verse.translation: Delusion is the root of all diseases, and from it spring many pains. Desire is the wind, greed the endless phlegm, and anger the bile that keeps the chest burning.
verse.why: Know your mind's diseases by name: confusion, anger, greed, envy, ego.

prasang.title: Garuda's seven questions
prasang.summary: Garuda asks seven questions: the rarest body, the greatest sorrow and joy, the nature of good and wicked people, the highest virtue and the worst wrong, and the diseases of the mind. Kakbhushundi answers: no sorrow like want, no joy like meeting good people; non-harm is highest and slander worst; delusion is the root disease, with lust, greed, anger, envy and ego as its symptoms.
prasang.lesson: Know your mind's diseases by name: confusion, anger, greed, envy, ego.

verse.for_you: Something someone did stays with you, and you feel like you will never be loved without being abandoned. That pain is a weight you carry, but it is not the whole of you.
verse.try_today: Notice the bile of anger. Let it burn without adding more fuel to the fire.

why: The illnesses of the mind (Ramcharitmanas, Uttar Kand 121-122 (Gita Press))
the many pains are given one root

verse.ref: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Draupadi and Yudhishthira
verse.speaker: Draupadi
verse.setting: Draupadi argues that waiting on fate is no plan: people must act.
verse.sanskrit: न त्वेवात्माऽवमन्तव्यः पुरुषेण कदाचन / न ह्यात्मपरिभूतस् भूतिर्भवति शोभना
verse.line: Never look down on yourself. Nothing good grows from self-contempt.
verse.translation: A person should never look down on himself. The one who despises himself never finds real prosperity.
verse.why: Do right for its own sake, then work as if it all depends on you.

prasang.title: Do right without reward, and keep working
prasang.summary: Draupadi questions a world where the good suffer; Yudhishthira answers that he does right because it is right, not for reward. Draupadi replies that effort still matters: fate rewards no one who waits.
prasang.lesson: Do right for its own sake, then work as if it all depends on you.

verse.try_today: Notice one moment when you treated yourself with fairness today.

why: Do not push yourself down; never hold yourself in contempt.
Self-reproach is shown to block every good

verse.speaker: Ram
verse.setting: Ram explains why he trusts the one who turns up at his door.
verse.sanskrit: पापवंत कर सहज सुभाऊ। भजनु मोर तेहि भाव न काऊ॥ जौं पै दुष्ट हृदय सोइ होई। मोरें सनमुख आव कि सोई ॥
verse.line: If they were truly wicked, would they have turned toward me at all?
verse.translation: It is the natural way of a sinner never to like worshipping me. If he were truly wicked at heart, would he come before me at all?
verse.why: The turning itself is enough to be taken in; your past is not the deciding question.

prasang.title: Vibhishan crosses over: Ram's refuge speech
prasang.summary: Kicked out of Lanka for telling his brother the truth, Vibhishan crosses the sea to Ram, dreaming of his feet. Sugriva wants him bound as a spy; Ram says his vow is to remove the fear of anyone who comes for refuge, and if the visitor were truly wicked he would not have come at all. Ram embraces him, asks how he kept his goodness among the cruel, describes the devotee who ties every thread of love to him, and crowns him king, shyly giving what Ravana got for ten heads.
prasang.story_hook: Kicked out by his own brother, a man stood on the far shore and wondered whether the enemy he was walking toward would let him in.
prasang.lesson: The turning itself is enough to be taken in; your past is not the deciding question.

verse.for_you: Something someone did stays with you. You do not need to be wicked in heart to have turned toward love. The one who comes to the door is already counted.
verse.try_today: Notice who shows up at your door today.

why: the turning toward him is itself evidence of the heart
having come at all counts for him

verse.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
verse.setting: 'The Common Bases of Hinduism', Lahore, November 1897.
verse.line: Learn everything that is good from others, but bring it in, and in your own way absorb it; do not become others.
verse.translation: Learn everything that is good from others, but bring it in, and in your own way absorb it; do not become others.
verse.why: Absorb the best of where you live, and grow into yourself.

prasang.title: Learn from all, imitate none (Lahore, 1897)
prasang.summary: Speaking to rival reform and orthodox groups, he looks for common ground. Religion must be realised, not repeated like a parrot. Learn everything good from others, as a seed takes in earth, air and water, but grow into your own tree and do not become others.
prasang.lesson: Absorb the best of where you live, and grow into yourself.

verse.try_today: Notice one thing you learned today and let it remain yours alone.

why: stay yourself while learning

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on being your own friend and staying steady in honour and insult.
verse.sanskrit: उद्धरेदात्मनाऽऽत्मानं नात्मानमवसादयेत् । आत्मैव ह्यात्मनो बन्धुरात्मैव रिपुरात्मनः ॥
verse.line: Be on your own side. Lift yourself up, don't push yourself down. You can be your own friend.
verse.translation: Raise yourself by your own self; do not let yourself sink. For the self alone is the friend of the self, and the self alone is the enemy of the self.
verse.why: You can be your own best friend or worst enemy; choose friend.
verse.misuse: Not 'you're alone, so don't ask for help'. Arjuna himself asks for help; this is about not abandoning yourself.

prasang.title: Lift yourself by yourself; marks of the realised
prasang.summary: Raise yourself by yourself; you are your own friend or enemy. The self-mastered person stays calm in heat and cold, praise and blame, and sees friend and foe alike.
prasang.lesson: You can be your own best friend or worst enemy; choose friend.

verse.meaning: A person must lift themselves up by their own effort and must not let themselves sink. The self is the only friend, and the self is the only enemy. No outside force can do this for you.
verse.for_you: The hurt of being abandoned can feel like proof you are not lovable. But this verse says you are the one with the power to lift yourself. You can be your own steady friend today.
verse.try_today: Notice one moment today when you choose not to push yourself down.

why: self-respect: you are the one who can lift you
Lift yourself by yourself

story.title: The last day of waiting
story.story_hook: There was one day left, and Bharat had begun to wonder whether he had been forgotten.
story.summary: One day is left of the fourteen years and there is no word. Bharat wonders whether Ram has forgotten him, and his mind starts to sink. Just then Hanuman arrives like a boat and says Ram is coming. Bharat says no gift could repay this news.
story.lesson: Waiting is hardest on the last day; hope can arrive just as you go under.
story.hook_title: One day was left, and Bharat began to wonder if Ram had forgotten him
story.teaser: One day was left, and Bharat began to wonder if Ram had forgotten him
story.for_you: You feel you will only be loved if you are abandoned. The waiting has turned into self-blame. You do not need to look at your own record right now.

why: When waiting turns into self-blame, lean on what you know of the other's nature, not on your own record.

verse.speaker: Bharat
verse.setting: Bharat, urged by his teacher and mother to accept the throne, explains why he cannot.
verse.sanskrit: तुम्ह तौ देहु सरल सिख सोई। जो आचरत मोर भल होई॥ जद्यपि यह समुझत हउँ नीकें। तदपि होत परितोष न जी कें ॥
verse.line: I understand your advice perfectly. My heart still isn't at peace.
verse.translation: You give me simple advice, the kind that would do me good if I followed it. Though I understand it well, my heart is not at peace.
verse.why: When head and heart disagree, go and face the person you think you wronged.

prasang.title: Bharat refuses the throne
prasang.summary: After the funeral, Vasishtha, the ministers and Kausalya all urge Bharat to rule, as his father wished. Bharat says the advice is right and his heart still isn't at peace; the crown means nothing without Ram. He decides to go to the forest, admit his fault, and trust his brother to forgive.
prasang.story_hook: Everyone agreed the throne was his, and Bharat could not bring himself to sit on it.
prasang.lesson: When head and heart disagree, go and face the person you think you wronged.

verse.for_you: You know the words that are supposed to help, and you still feel the weight of what was done. Understanding does not lift the hurt. Let the ache be where it is for now, without asking it to leave.
verse.try_today: Notice the exact moment when advice lands in your mind but not in your chest.

why: Everyone must think I wanted this. I can't look at anyone. Will he even see me?
understanding does not reach the grief

verse.speaker: A brahmin (retold by Bhishma)
verse.setting: The brahmin explains to King Senajit why loss hurts so much.
verse.sanskrit: किंचिदेव ममत्वेन यदा भवति कल्पितम् / तदेव परितापाय नाशे संपद्यते तदा
verse.line: Whatever you start calling 'mine' becomes a source of pain the day you lose it.
verse.translation: Whatever a person begins to think of as 'mine', that very thing becomes a source of anguish when it is lost.
verse.why: No one suffers forever. Meet what comes with an undefeated heart.

prasang.title: King Senajit and the brahmin's consolation
prasang.summary: King Senajit is crushed by his son's death. A brahmin comforts him: everyone suffers, no sorrow lasts forever, effort beats idleness, and whatever we call 'mine' becomes a source of pain.
prasang.lesson: No one suffers forever. Meet what comes with an undefeated heart.

verse.for_you: You feel like you will never be loved without being abandoned. The grip on that hope is what hurts. Let it go.
verse.try_today: Notice one thing you are holding onto today and let your hands relax around it.
verse.scene_line: You stand in the ruins of her waiting, and the brahmin speaks of what is called mine.

why: The night she stopped waiting (Mahabharata, Shanti Parva 173-174 (Gita Press))
Shows the sense of 'mine' as the handle by which loss hurts
plan_v3.writer_note: Letting-go teaching for a reader who is young and afraid of being left. Explain it through their own situation and feeling: what is released is the grip that hurts them, never their love, their hope or their work. Never say or imply 'stop caring' or 'your hope is the problem'. Read it after the guard verse, which reassures first.

guard.line: Every living being is an eternal part of me, says Krishna.

verse.speaker: Uddalaka Aruni
verse.setting: The refrain closing each of Uddalaka's lessons.
verse.sanskrit: स य एषोऽणिमैतदात्म्यमिदꣳ सर्वं तत्सत्यꣳ स आत्मा तत्त्वमसि श्वेतकेतो इति भूय एव मा भगवान्विज्ञापयत्विति तथा सोम्येति होवाच ॥
verse.line: That subtle essence is the self of all that is. That is truth. You are that, Shvetaketu.
verse.translation: That which is the subtle essence: this whole world has it as its self. That is the truth. That is the self. That you are, Shvetaketu. 'Teach me more, sir.' 'So be it, dear one.'
verse.why: What is most real in you is unseen, everywhere, and the same in all.

prasang.title: Uddalaka's lessons: tat tvam asi
prasang.summary: Uddalaka teaches his son through everyday experiments: a fast that dims the mind, a bird on a string, rivers merging in the sea, a banyan seed with nothing visible inside, salt dissolved in water, a blindfolded man finding his way home. Each lesson ends: 'That subtle essence is the self of all. You are that, Shvetaketu.'
prasang.lesson: What is most real in you is unseen, everywhere, and the same in all.

verse.for_you: You feel you will never be loved without being abandoned, and something stays with you. The verse says the subtle essence is the self of all that is. You are not small.
verse.try_today: Notice when the feeling of abandonment speaks, and return to the idea that you are that subtle essence.
verse.scene_line: You stand in the room where the hurt happened, while the banyan seed and the rivers teach you who you are.

why: the self the verse points to is not the one that failed
What you are is not small.

verse.speaker: Teacher
verse.setting: A catechism of definitions: 'What is caste?'
verse.sanskrit: जातिरिति च न चर्मणो न रक्तस्य न मांसस्य न चास्थिनः । न जातिरात्मनो जातिर्व्यवहारप्रकल्पिता ।
verse.line: Caste is not in skin, blood, flesh or bone. The self has no caste; caste is a social convention.
verse.translation: And what is caste? It is not of the skin, nor of the blood, nor of the flesh, nor of the bones. The self has no caste; caste is a convention made for worldly dealings.
verse.for_you: A label fixed at birth has no hold on what you are. You are not that hurt, and you are not that label.
verse.try_today: Notice when a label tries to define your worth today.
verse.scene_line: The self has no caste, and neither do you.

why: shame about origin has nothing in the self to attach to
a label fixed at birth is denied any hold on what one is

verse.speaker: Ram
verse.setting: Ram to Sugriva on the marks of a good friend.
verse.sanskrit: देत लेत मन संक न धरई। बल अनुमान सदा हित करई॥ बिपति काल कर सतगुन नेहा। श्रुति कह संत मित्र गुन एहा ॥
verse.line: A good friend gives without keeping score, and loves you a hundredfold more in hard times.
verse.translation: He gives and takes without suspicion, always does you good as far as he is able, and in hard times loves you a hundred times more. These, say the scriptures, are the qualities of a good friend.
verse.why: A friend treats your trouble as bigger than their own.

prasang.title: Ram and Sugriva become friends
prasang.summary: Hanuman, sent to check whether the two strangers are Bali's spies, recognises Ram and brings him to Sugriva, who has been driven out by his brother. Before a fire as witness they become friends, and Ram describes what friendship asks: your friend's small trouble is a mountain, your own is dust; steer him right, hide his faults, love him more in hard times.
prasang.lesson: A friend treats your trouble as bigger than their own.

verse.for_you: You are studying and feeling that old hurt still lives inside you. A good friend gives without keeping score, and loves you a hundredfold more in hard times. Let this be your measure for how you might let yourself be held.
verse.try_today: Notice one moment today when someone gives you something without keeping score.
verse.scene_line: You stand in your study, feeling the weight of past abandonment, while Ram and Sugriva stand before the fire as new friends.

why: giving and taking without misgiving
love that multiplies in the friend's bad time

verse.speaker: Vasishtha
verse.setting: Vasishtha on the fourth gatekeeper: good company (satsanga).
verse.sanskrit: अपि कष्टतरां प्राप्तैर्दशां विवशतां गतैः । मनागपि न संत्याज्या मानवैः साधुसंगतिः ॥
verse.line: Even at your lowest and most helpless, don't let go of good company.
verse.translation: Even when people fall into the hardest straits and feel helpless, they should not let go of good company, not even a little.
verse.why: Pick one of calm, clear thinking, contentment or good company. Grow it, and the others follow.

prasang.title: The four gatekeepers: calm, inquiry, contentment, good company
prasang.summary: Vasishtha tells Rama that four gatekeepers guard the door to freedom: calm, inquiry, contentment and good company. He gives a chapter to each, then says you only need to start with one, because each one strengthens the others.
prasang.lesson: Pick one of calm, clear thinking, contentment or good company. Grow it, and the others follow.

verse.for_you: The hurt you carry is real and heavy. You do not have to hold it alone. Stay close to those who steady you today.
verse.try_today: Notice one person who steadies you and let them stay near.
verse.scene_line: You stand in the middle of your study, and you remember the people who have stayed with you.

why: holding to those who steady you

story.title: Tulsidas, the boy who begged for scraps
story.story_hook: The poet of the Ramcharitmanas began life as an unwanted child begging for scraps in the lanes.
story.summary: Across his later works Tulsidas tells his own story: left by his parents at birth, he wandered door to door for scraps, no job, no trade, no skill, ignored by everyone. Good people told him not to worry; Hanuman raised him like a child; Ram's name, he says, turned a thorny babul into a mango tree. Even when he went astray, he was taken back.
story.lesson: Where you start is not where you end; you can be taken in from nothing.
story.hook_title: Tulsidas began life as an unwanted child begging for scraps
story.teaser: Tulsidas began life as an unwanted child begging for scraps
story.for_you: The hurt of being left is still with you, and that is real. You do not have to earn care by being perfect. One honest asking is enough to be met.
